# Thesis: investors are slow to price how oil moves feed into earnings; stocks with a positive own oil beta keep rising after a quarter of oil gains (and fall after oil declines), so go long beta x sign(60-day oil change).
# Critic fix (Oct 7): see alphas/drafts/c4-newdata.critic.md
# Source: "Oil Price Exposure and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns" (Penn State working paper, slow reaction to lagged quarterly oil changes, Sharpe 0.50), https://pure.psu.edu/en/publications/oil-price-exposure-and-the-cross-section-of-stock-returns/
f = close/close  # float32 ones matrix for dtype-safe flags
oilchg = ts_diff(wti_spot_crude_oil_price, 1)  # daily oil price change (correlation is scale-free, works even for negative prices)
beta = ts_corr_binary(ret1, oilchg, 250)  # each stock's one-year correlation with oil moves: stock-specific oil exposure
mkt = ts_corr_binary(ret1, ret1_spx, 250)  # one-year market correlation, removed so the leg is not plain beta
o1 = ts_delay(wti_spot_crude_oil_price, 1)  # yesterday's oil price (today's EIA print may not be out by the close)
updn = f*(o1 > ts_delay(o1, 60)) - f*(o1 < ts_delay(o1, 60))
sig = cs_factorneut(cs_zscore(beta), [cs_zscore(mkt)])  # oil exposure orthogonal to market exposure
alpha = cs_indneut(sig*updn, industry)  # within-industry oil-response bet, direction set by the last quarter's oil move

# Thesis: gold is the crash/tail-risk hedge; stocks whose returns co-move with gold are hedges investors overpay for, so high gold-beta stocks earn lower future returns and low gold-beta stocks higher.
# Source: Huang & Kilic, "Gold, Platinum, and Expected Stock Returns" (Journal of Financial Economics 2019), https://conference.nber.org/conf_papers/f80928.pdf
gbeta = ts_corr_binary(ret1, ret1_gld, 250)  # one-year correlation of each stock with daily gold returns (stock-specific hedge value)
mbeta = ts_corr_binary(ret1, ret1_spx, 250)  # one-year market correlation, a control so gold beta is not a market-beta proxy
sig = cs_factorneut(-cs_zscore(gbeta), [cs_zscore(mbeta)])  # short gold hedges, long gold-insensitive names, beyond market beta
alpha = cs_indneut(sig, industry)  # compare only within industry so miners vs non-miners is not the whole bet

# Thesis: news about future GDP growth is a priced risk factor; stocks whose returns load on real-time growth news must pay a premium, so long high GDP-news beta, short low (hedges), beyond market beta.
# Critic fix (Oct 7): see alphas/drafts/c4-newdata.critic.md
# Source: Vassalou, "News Related to Future GDP Growth as a Risk Factor in Equity Returns" (Journal of Financial Economics 2003), https://business.columbia.edu/sites/default/files-efs/pubfiles/627/gdpjfe.pdf
g = ts_delay(gdp_now_annualized_percent_change, 1)  # yesterday's GDPNow (published values only; pre-Jul-2014 is a backcast, trust post-2014 results)
gnews = g - ts_delay(g, 5)
gbeta = ts_corr_binary(ret5, gnews, 250)  # one-year correlation of each stock's weekly return with growth news
mbeta = ts_corr_binary(ret1, ret1_spx, 250)  # one-year market correlation, removed so this is not plain beta
sig = cs_factorneut(cs_zscore(gbeta), [cs_zscore(mbeta)])  # growth-news exposure orthogonal to market exposure
alpha = cs_indneut(sig, industry)  # within-industry: stock-specific growth sensitivity, not sector cyclicality

# Thesis: index/ETF money concentrates its trading at the close while disagreement-driven trading happens through the day; the share of volume traded at the close is a stock-level disagreement/ownership trait that predicts returns, so long stocks with a high closing-volume share vs industry peers.
# Source: Bogousslavsky & Muravyev, "Who Trades at the Close? Implications for Price Discovery and Liquidity" (AEA 2021 / Journal of Financial Markets 2023; auction-to-total volume predicts returns), https://aeaweb.org/conference/2021/preliminary/paper/H9T4hef7
csh = volume_last_hour/(volume_first_hour + volume_last_hour)  # daily share of open+close-hour volume traded in the last hour (dimensionless)
lvl = ts_mean(csh, 60)  # 3-month average closing share: a slow stock-level trait
tsz = ts_mean((volume_first_hour + volume_last_hour)/(number_of_trades_first_hour + number_of_trades_last_hour), 60)/ts_mean((volume_first_hour + volume_last_hour)/(number_of_trades_first_hour + number_of_trades_last_hour), 250)  # trade-size trend, a control (our ID_TSIZE legs failed alone)
sig = cs_factorneut(cs_zscore(lvl), [cs_zscore(tsz), cs_zscore(at_signlog(mktcap))])  # closing share beyond size (index membership) and trade-size drift
alpha = cs_indneut(sig, industry)  # within-industry; if Fast IR is clearly negative, the paper's sign reading is the reverse: flip once

# Thesis: stocks have persistent own-calendar return seasonalities; a stock that historically earns more around the turn of the month than on other days keeps doing so, so hold it only through the turn-of-month window.
# Critic fix (Oct 7): see alphas/drafts/c4-newdata.critic.md
# Source: Keloharju, Linnainmaa & Nyberg, "Return Seasonalities" (Journal of Finance 2016; seasonalities also at daily frequency), https://www.nber.org/papers/w20815.pdf
f = close/close  # float32 ones matrix for dtype-safe flags
tom = f*(days_until_last_trading_day_of_month <= 1) + f*(days_since_first_trading_day_of_month <= 2)  # today is in the turn-of-month window (last 2 + first 3 days), a known calendar fact
hist = ts_sum(ret1*tom, 250)/ts_sum(tom, 250) - ts_sum(ret1*(1 - tom), 250)/ts_sum(1 - tom, 250)  # past-year mean return inside minus outside the window, from realised returns only
nxt = f*(days_until_last_trading_day_of_month <= 2) + f*(days_since_first_trading_day_of_month <= 1)  # tomorrow falls in the window (scheduled calendar, no look-ahead)
h = cs_factorneut(cs_zscore(hist), [cs_zscore(ts_mean(ret1, 250))])  # seasonal edge net of the stock's average return
alpha = cs_indneut(h*(2*nxt - 1), industry)  # every day: long the seasonal names inside the window, short them outside (no flat days)

# Thesis: option hedging and pinning move optionable stocks by ~16 bp in expiration week, in a stock-specific direction tied to its option open interest; a stock's own past expiration-week excess return repeats, so hold it into each monthly expiration.
# Critic fix (Oct 7): see alphas/drafts/c4-newdata.critic.md
# Source: Ni, Pearson & Poteshman, "Stock Price Clustering on Option Expiration Dates" (Journal of Financial Economics 2005), https://scholars.hkbu.edu.hk/en/publications/stock-price-clustering-on-option-expiration-dates-3/
f = close/close  # float32 ones matrix for dtype-safe flags
wk = f*(days_until_next_monthly_options_expiration <= 4)  # today is in the expiration week (scheduled third-Friday calendar)
hist = ts_sum(ret1*wk, 250)/ts_sum(wk, 250) - ts_sum(ret1*(1 - wk), 250)/ts_sum(1 - wk, 250)  # past-year mean expiration-week return minus mean other-day return
nxt = f*(days_until_next_monthly_options_expiration <= 5) - f*(days_until_next_monthly_options_expiration <= 0)  # tomorrow is in the expiration week (1..5 days to go)
h = cs_factorneut(cs_zscore(hist), [cs_zscore(ts_mean(ret1, 250))])  # seasonal edge net of the stock's average return
alpha = cs_indneut(h*(2*nxt - 1), industry)  # every day: long the seasonal names inside the window, short them outside (no flat days)

# Thesis: distressed firms earn anomalously low returns and the market prices distress changes slowly; rising interest coverage and cash ratio mean falling failure risk, so long improving-solvency firms, short deteriorating ones.
# Source: Campbell, Hilscher & Szilagyi, "In Search of Distress Risk" (Journal of Finance 2008), https://www.nber.org/papers/w12362
cov = ts_fill(at_signlog(times_interest_earned_ratio))  # interest coverage (EBIT / interest), sign-log so losses and huge ratios stay comparable
cr = ts_fill(at_signlog(cash_ratio))  # cash / current liabilities, sign-log compressed
dcov = cov - ts_delay(cov, 120)  # 6-month change in log coverage
dcr = cr - ts_delay(cr, 120)  # 6-month change in log cash ratio
sig = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(cs_zscore(dcov)) + 0.5*at_nan2zero(cs_zscore(dcr)))  # coverage leads, liquidity adds; firms without interest expense keep the cash leg
alpha = cs_indneut(sig, industry)  # within-industry solvency improvement

# Thesis: the 6-month CHANGE in accumulated_other_comprehensive_income carries news that is under-reacted to (fundamental momentum). Field-sweep alpha (template D, class DOLLAR); sign +.
# Source: Green, Hand & Zhang, "The Characteristics that Provide Independent Information about Average U.S. Monthly Stock Returns" (Review of Financial Studies 2017), https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhx019; Hou, Xue & Zhang, "Replicating Anomalies" (Review of Financial Studies 2020), https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhy131
n = ts_fill(accumulated_other_comprehensive_income)/ts_fill(total_assets)  # accumulated_other_comprehensive_income scaled by total assets (dimensionless)
alpha = cs_rank(n - ts_delay(n, 120))  # 6-month change: improving minus deteriorating firms

alpha = cs_rank(n - ts_delay(n, 120))  # 6-month change: improving minus deteriorating firms
